title: The Drop of Vienna
premise: When Flight 407 to Vienna vanishes from every radar, manifest, and database while still airborne, hostage negotiator Silas Delacroix is summoned by a former colleague who shouldn't exist. The disappearance is no glitch: a private syndicate embedded in European aviation authorities is erasing the plane to stage a catastrophic 'accident' that will trigger a lucrative security contract, and the only witness to the conspiracy is the daughter of the man Silas failed to save fifteen years ago. Silas, a disgraced air marshal, and the stowaway daughter must board the ghost flight mid-crisis, expose the syndicate's mole inside the negotiation command center, and force the truth into the open before the plane is dropped from the sky. In the end, Silas chooses justice over protocol, broadcasting the cockpit recordings live as the syndicate's architect falls, and he finally forgives himself for the failure that defined him.
about_author: Marguerite Marchetti is a former airline operations analyst who spent a decade in European flight-control rooms before turning to fiction. She lives between Vienna and Trieste, writing thrillers about systems that fail the people they were built to protect.

chapters.title: Static on the Line
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Fifteen years after losing a hostage in Vienna, Silas teaches negotiation to recruits who mock his caution. A midnight call from Lena Vogel, a colleague officially dead since 2019, pulls him to a control center where Flight 407 exists on no screen. Beat: dread reawakened, the past knocking.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas learns the flight's manifest lists 212 souls, yet the airline denies the flight ever boarded. Among the names: Mara Kessler, daughter of the hostage he lost. Lena reveals records are being deleted from inside the authority. Beat: guilt sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Ghost Altitude
chapters.summary: POV Mara, aboard Flight 407. Mara, an aviation journalist chasing her father's cold case, notices the cabin crew lying about a diversion. Turbulence that isn't turbulence — a pressure test. She hides in a service galley and finds a stowaway: disgraced air marshal Tomas Reyes. Beat: isolation turning to alliance.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The syndicate offers Silas a deal: walk away, and his fifteen-year-old failure stays buried. He recognizes the negotiator's cadence in the voice — someone trained like him. Silas realizes the 'accident' is scheduled for dawn over the Alps. Beat: temptation refused, clock started.

chapters.title: The Man in Seat 4C
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara and Reyes identify the syndicate's onboard operative by his too-calm behavior during the pressure drop. A passenger dies of 'a heart attack' that isn't one. Mara steals the dead man's encrypted phone. Beat: fear transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Vienna Will Not Answer
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas and Lena trace the deletion orders to Deputy Director Halloran, Silas's old mentor, and discover the security contract worth billions. Lena is exposed and captured buying them time. Silas, alone now, must reach the plane. Beat: betrayal by the man who taught him the rules.

chapters.title: Descent Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Mara, then Reyes. The operative takes partial control of the aircraft via a backdoor transponder, and the autopilot begins a controlled descent toward an uninhabited valley. Mara broadcasts the encrypted phone's data to any frequency still listening. Beat: the drop begins, hope a thin signal.

chapters.title: Negotiation at 30,000 Feet
chapters.summary: POV Silas, aboard via hijacked radio. Silas does what he does best: he negotiates with the operative, using Halloran's voiceprint and the broadcast signal as leverage, stalling the descent while Reyes reaches the avionics bay. Beat: mastery under pressure, the failure haunting every choice.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: POV all three, interwoven. Reyes kills the backdoor; the operative, cornered, tries to force a crash. Silas talks the operative down by naming his own failure aloud — the confession he's withheld for fifteen years. The plane levels. Mara's data goes live worldwide. Beat: climax, redemption through honesty.

chapters.title: What the Records Keep
chapters.summary: POV Silas, epilogue. Halloran falls; the syndicate unravels in hearings Mara's footage ignited. Lena is restored to the living. Silas visits the Kessler grave with Mara beside him — not as penance, but as family. He returns to teaching, teaching them to break rules for people. Beat: found family, justice, peace.
